title: DOJ Sues 31 States for Voter Rolls While Threatening Officials with Arrest
description_short: DOJ Sues 31 States for Voter Rolls While Threatening Officials with Arrest
description_medium: The packet says the Justice Department sued election officials in 31 states seeking unredacted voter-registration data, including Social Security numbers. It also describes later threats to withhold federal funds or arrest officials who did not remove voters flagged by a federal system. The linked AP article concerns the litigation, but the packet’s claims about a year-long SAVE database plan, 67 million records, and court rulings require their own linked evidence.
description_long: By April 2026, internal DOJ communications obtained by CNN revealed the Trump administration had been working for nearly a year on a covert plan to use DHS's SAVE citizenship database to identify and remove noncitizens from voter rolls, while hiding the plan's details from courts and Democratic election officials. The DOJ had brought lawsuits against the election chiefs of 31 states — primarily Democratic — demanding unredacted voter registration data including Social Security numbers, arguing noncompliance violated federal law. By July 2026, AP News reported the administration was threatening to withhold federal funding from states and warning state election officials they faced arrest if they did not remove voters flagged by the federal system — despite multiple courts having rejected the efforts as based on 'untrue claims about widespread voting fraud.' At least 67 million voter registrations had been run through federal databases with tens of thousands flagged, including documented cases of U.S. citizens wrongly identified by the SAVE system.

title: CNN Reports OPM Fired Privacy, Communications and FOIA Staff
description_short: CNN Reports OPM Fired Privacy, Communications and FOIA Staff
description_medium: A CNN report republished by ABC17 on February 18, 2025 said the Trump administration fired members of the Office of Personnel Management's privacy team, communications staff, and employees handling FOIA requests. CNN had sought records about security clearances for Elon Musk and DOGE personnel with access to sensitive networks; an OPM email replied, “Good luck with that, they just fired the whole privacy team.” The report documents OPM dismissals, not a government-wide dismantling of FOIA operations.
description_long: A CNN report republished by ABC17 on February 18, 2025 said the Trump administration quietly dismissed several members of the Office of Personnel Management's privacy team and other officials. CNN learned of the firings while seeking records about security clearances for Elon Musk and Department of Government Efficiency personnel who had access to sensitive or classified networks. In response to CNN's FOIA request, an OPM email account reportedly wrote: “Good luck with that, they just fired the whole privacy team.” The report also attributed the firing of OPM communications staff and employees who handle FOIA requests to two sources familiar with the matter. It noted that firing staff does not remove the government's legal duty to respond to records requests. This account supports an OPM-specific report about records access and staffing. The supplied link does not establish DOGE firing FOIA officers across federal agencies or the separate Presidential Records Act, court-order, and National Archives chronology in the prior long description; those claims have been removed pending event-specific sources.
notes: The supplied ABC17 page republishes CNN's February 18, 2025 report. Its text names OPM's privacy team, communications staff, and FOIA employees; explains CNN's request for Musk/DOGE security-clearance records; and quotes the agency response. The article supports an OPM-focused description but not the prior government-wide FOIA and Presidential Records Act claims, which are removed.
proposed_correction: Keep the original long field unchanged, but source each separate FOIA and records-retention event; distinguish the OPM privacy-team firing from wider workforce cuts.
